audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. The displayed collar homotopy exits the tube; Equation (6.1) has no uniform absolute error; Lemma 6.4 lacks a boundary membership hypothesis
limitations: Counterevidence: Formula works for linear collars; bottom limit is correct. Neither controls intermediate t. Positive-orientation example does not depend on P4.
Counterevidence: Main round-Clifford use needs only one-sided lower bound; Jacobian <=sec(2r) gives area>=cos(2r) area(C). Oscillatory examples not claimed F-close as required later.
Counterevidence: Prop6.5 explicitly includes boundary target membership.
Counterevidence: Main near-minimal application is oriented and F-close; author Goeritz group concerns handlebody-preserving diffeomorphisms.
Counterevidence: Both formal orientations of the unoriented single torus give two points, but that is another space.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.

proposition.claim:
Normalized collar scaling remains in T^2 x [-r,r]

Absolute area-projected-mass difference <= Lambda r^2 for any smooth closed surface in tube

Boundary equality with g into isometric orbit under only F-closeness

All globally isotopic essential embeddings in tube connect to fixed oriented target

Connected identity group quotient is two points when q!=1
